questions.q: A p+ extension is implanted with 11B+ at 10 keV (Rp ~ 37 nm, delta-Rp ~ 17 nm) to a dose of 1e15 cm^-2. Roughly what is the as-implanted peak boron concentration?
questions.explanation: For a Gaussian profile the peak is Np = Q / (sqrt(2*pi) * delta-Rp) = 0.4 * 1e15 / 1.7e-6 cm = 2.4e20 cm^-3, which is right at boron's solid-solubility limit; this is why 1e15 cm^-2 is the canonical high dose.

questions.q: Why does a 1,050 C spike anneal lasting under a second often produce LESS boron diffusion than an 800 C anneal for 10 minutes?
options: Boron diffusivity is lower at 1,050 C than at 800 C
Transient enhanced diffusion from dissolving {311} interstitial defects is worse at lower temperature because the interstitials are released slowly instead of annihilating quickly at the surface
The spike anneal melts the surface so dopants cannot move
At 800 C boron pairs with vacancies and becomes highly mobile
questions.explanation: TED is driven by the excess silicon interstitials left by the implant; at 700-900 C the {311} defects release them slowly over minutes and boron diffusivity is enhanced 1,000x, while a spike anneal gets through the transient in under a second.

questions.q: A high-current implanter runs in deceleration mode: ions are extracted at 5 keV and slowed to 500 eV before the wafer. What is the specific risk this creates and how do modern tools mitigate it?
options: Space charge blows up the beam; mitigated by a plasma flood gun
The Faraday cup over-counts dose; mitigated by a suppression electrode
Channeling increases; mitigated by 7 degree tilt
Energy contamination: ions neutralised by charge exchange before the decel stage arrive at the full 5 keV and land ~ 10x deeper; mitigated by a bend or energy filter after deceleration
questions.explanation: A neutral cannot be decelerated by the electrostatic decel stage, so a few percent of the beam arriving at 10x the intended energy creates a deep tail that sets the junction depth; placing the energy filter after the decel stage removes anything not at the final energy.

questions.q: Which statement about the analyser magnet is correct? A 49 amu BF2+ ion at 30 keV is selected instead of 11B+ because...
options: BF2+ has a higher charge state so it gains more energy per volt
BF2+ delivers its boron atom at only about 30 x (11/49) = 6.7 keV, giving a shallower profile than the tool could otherwise reach, and the heavy fragments amorphise the surface as they go
BF2+ is the only boron-bearing ion produced in a BF3 plasma
Fluorine acts as a donor and compensates the boron
questions.explanation: The molecular ion shares its kinetic energy among its atoms in proportion to mass, so a 30 keV BF2+ implant is effectively a 6.7 keV boron implant with a self-amorphising fluorine co-implant; the same principle is used by B18H22 cluster ions.

questions.q: Why are the channels of modern FinFET and nanosheet transistors left undoped, with threshold voltage set by gate work-function metals rather than a channel implant?
options: At 1e18 cm^-3 a 20 nm x 20 nm x 20 nm channel contains only ~ 8 dopant atoms, so Poisson statistics (random dopant fluctuation) would make the threshold voltage uncontrollable
Implanters cannot reach the 1e17-1e18 cm^-3 doping range
Dopants in the channel would diffuse into the gate oxide during the anneal
The high-k dielectric is destroyed by any implant
questions.explanation: 1e18 cm^-3 x (20 nm)^3 = 8 atoms, with a +/-35 % statistical spread; fully depleted fins and sheets do not need channel doping for electrostatics, so the industry moved V_T control to TiN/TiAl/dipole layers in the metal gate.

questions.q: Silicon carbide power MOSFETs are implanted with aluminium at ~ 500 C wafer temperature and annealed at 1,600-1,800 C under a carbon cap. Why is each of these three unusual conditions necessary?
options: Hot implant increases beam current; the high anneal temperature drives the Al deep; the carbon cap adds n-type dopant
Hot implant reduces channeling; the high temperature dissolves {311} defects; the carbon cap acts as an anti-reflective layer

Hot implant prevents amorphisation (amorphous SiC does not regrow in the correct polytype); ~ 1,700 C is needed to activate Al because dopants barely diffuse or activate in SiC below that; the carbon cap stops the SiC surface subliming and step-bunching
All three are only needed because SiC wafers are 150 mm rather than 300 mm
questions.explanation: Diffusion in SiC is negligible, so every doped region must be implanted to its final shape and activated at extreme temperature; amorphised SiC recrystallises as defective 3C material, and bare SiC loses silicon by sublimation above ~ 1,500 C, hence the graphitised-photoresist cap.

questions.q: Boron's equilibrium diffusivity at 800 C is about 4e-17 cm^2/s, so a 10-minute anneal should give a wander distance sqrt(Dt) of only ~1.6 nm. Yet a 1e14 cm^-2 boron implant annealed at 800 C for 10 minutes moves ~50 nm. Roughly what enhancement of the diffusivity does this imply, and what causes it?
options: ~30x, caused by the surface oxide injecting vacancies
~1,000x, caused by the excess silicon interstitials released from dissolving {311} defects (transient enhanced diffusion)
~30,000x, caused by boron melting the surface
~1,000,000x, caused by channeling during the implant
questions.explanation: The wander distance scales as the square root of D, so moving 32x further (50 nm / 1.6 nm) needs about 32^2 = 1,000x the diffusivity. That is the interstitial supersaturation of 1e3-1e4 created when the implant's excess interstitials, stored in {311} defects, dissolve over minutes at 700-950 C.

questions.q: A four-point probe on the monitor wafer from a 5e14 cm^-2 arsenic source/drain implant reads V/I = 61.8 ohm after the spike anneal. Full activation at ~1e20 cm^-3 (mobility ~90 cm^2/V.s) would give ~140 ohm/sq. What does the reading tell the process engineer? For this diagnostic estimate, assume the carrier mobility and profile shape match the reference.
options: R_s = 4.532 x 61.8 = 280 ohm/sq, i.e. only ~50 % of the dose is active; suspect a cold anneal or dopant clustering
R_s = 61.8 ohm/sq, so the implant was over-dosed by about 2x
R_s = 280 ohm/sq, so the junction is twice as deep as intended
The probe cannot read arsenic layers; a SIMS profile is required
questions.explanation: Sheet resistance is R_s = (pi/ln 2) x V/I = 4.532 x 61.8 = 280 ohm/sq, twice the fully activated value. Since R_s = 1/(q x Q_active x mobility), twice the resistance means half the active dose (about 50 % activation); if the pre-anneal ThermaProbe reading was normal, the implanter delivered the dose and the anneal is the suspect. In production, mobility and profile changes can also change sheet resistance, so this measurement alone does not uniquely determine activation.
